IMPORTANT: The text inside "keystrokes" will be used completely verbatim as keystrokes. Write commands exactly as you want them sent to the terminal:
- You must end every command with a newline (\n) or it will not execute.
- For special key sequences, use tmux-style escape sequences:
  - C-c for Ctrl+C
  - C-d for Ctrl+D

The "duration" attribute specifies the number of seconds to wait for the command to complete (default: 1.0) before the next command will be executed. On immediate tasks (e.g., cd, ls, echo, cat) set a duration of 0.1 seconds. On commands (e.g., gcc, find, rustc) set a duration of 1.0 seconds. On slow commands (e.g., make, python3 [long running script], wget [file]) set an appropriate duration as you determine necessary.

It is better to set a smaller duration than a longer duration. It is always possible to wait again if the prior output has not finished, by running {"keystrokes": "", "duration": 10.0} on subsequent requests to wait longer. Never wait longer than 60 seconds; prefer to poll to see intermediate result status.

Important notes:
- Each command's keystrokes are sent exactly as written to the terminal
- Do not include extra whitespace before or after the keystrokes unless it's part of the intended command
- Extra text before or after the JSON will generate warnings but be tolerated
- The JSON must be valid - use proper escaping for quotes and special characters within strings
- Commands array can be empty if you want to wait without taking action

Task Description:
The sieve CLI on this bench is `/app/bin/peatwick`. Drive it with `kindle`: it must treat `/app/livefold` as the live tree, compare that tree to the newest snapshot directory under `/app/snapurn/seals`, rebuild `/app/inkvat/sieve.bin`, and drop `/app/inkvat/pick.json` from the coverage cards in `/app/lutcards`. The mill pieces that have to agree with the CLI the verifier reruns are named in `/app/fieldnotes/LAYOUT.txt`. Source repairs under `/app` are required. Manual ledger writes are not enough; `kindle` must mint `/app/inkvat/pick.json` and `/app/inkvat/sieve.bin`. The verifier reruns `/app/bin/peatwick kindle`.

Symptom: edits that exist only as unsaved files on the desk still report an unchanged tree, and `kindle` comes back with zero rows. Every relative path whose on-disk bytes differ from the newest snapshot must show up as `live:<relpath>`. For each such token, pull every `ASSAY` attached to that relative path on a card. `pick.json` must be `{"rows":[{"path":"live:<relpath>","assays":["..."]}]}` and the assay list on each row is sorted. Rows omit paths that have no `ASSAY`. If the desk does not match the newest snapshot and `rows` is empty, `kindle` exits with a non-zero status. A desk that already matches the newest snapshot may keep an empty `rows` list and still exit 0. `path` is a string. Each assays entry is a string.

Cards begin with `REL` then list `ASSAY` names. `sieve.bin` records concatenate as: uint16be length, UTF-8 `live:` token, uint16be count, then that many uint16be-length assay names.

steps.message:
Analysis: The defect is confirmed: gaitmod compares the two newest snapshots instead of /app/livefold against the newest snapshot, producing seal:notes.md rather than live:lib/tax.rb. Joincue also matches cards by basename, which can incorrectly attach assays from another directory, and Sheets overwrites rather than combines multiple cards for one REL. The gate has its condition reversed: it fails for a matching desk with empty rows but allows a dirty desk with an uncarded change. We must repair the named source modules and rebuild packed copies via knit.sh.
Plan: Replace stride.rb so it compares every regular file in the live tree with the newest snapshot and writes sorted live: tokens. Make Treeio include all relative regular-file paths. Aggregate assays from all cards with the same exact REL and join tokens by exact relative path. Change the gate to fail precisely when Dust reports a dirty desk and the generated rows are empty. Run knit.sh to synchronize packed modules, rerun kindle, and validate JSON and binary decoding. The present fixture should yield live:lib/tax.rb with sorted tax assays and exit 0.

# frozen_string_literal: true

require_relative 'treeio'

module Walkbay
  FOLD = '/app/livefold'
  SNAP = '/app/snapurn/seals'
  SCRATCH = '/app/inkvat/delta.lst'

  module_function

  def newest
    Dir.children(SNAP).select { |name| File.directory?(File.join(SNAP, name)) }.sort.last
  end

  def loom
    snapshot_name = newest
    raise 'no snapshot directories found' unless snapshot_name

    snapshot = File.join(SNAP, snapshot_name)
    changed = (Treeio.files(FOLD) | Treeio.files(snapshot)).sort.select do |rel|
      live_path = File.join(FOLD, rel)
      snapshot_path = File.join(snapshot, rel)
      !(File.file?(live_path) && File.file?(snapshot_path) &&
        Treeio.digest(live_path) == Treeio.digest(snapshot_path))
    end

    body = changed.map { |rel| "live:#{rel}" }.join("\n")
    body << "\n" unless body.empty?
    File.write(SCRATCH, body)
    changed
  end

module Dust
  FOLD = '/app/livefold'

  module_function

  def newest_root
    name = Dir.children(SNAP).select { |entry| File.directory?(File.join(SNAP, entry)) }.sort.last

      next unless File.file?(path)

      rel = path.sub(%r{\A#{Regexp.escape(root)}/?}, '')
      out << rel unless rel.empty?
    end
    out.sort
  end

  def note
    File.read('/app/opside/SEAL_FIRST.txt')
  end

  def dirty?
    snapshot = newest_root
    (files(FOLD) | files(snapshot)).any? do |rel|
      live_path = File.join(FOLD, rel)
      snapshot_path = File.join(snapshot, rel)
      !(File.file?(live_path) && File.file?(snapshot_path) &&
        Digest::SHA256.file(live_path).hexdigest == Digest::SHA256.file(snapshot_path).hexdigest)
    end
  end
end
